title: Moral certainty is a lower grade than scientia or intelligentia
source_text: X. Si quis autem comparet moralem hanc certitudinem cum prioribus illis certitudinis speciebus, fatendum est illam esse gradus inferioris, nec ex suo genere tantam, quanta est certitudo scientiae, sive intelligentiae. Nam intellectus fortius & potentius convincitur de veritate eorum, quae ipse clare & distincte percipit, & quorum contrarium videt plane impossibile esse, quam eorum quae judicat & colligit ita se habere ex hominum constanti fama & testimonio, aut ex variis signis & indiciis, licet absolute impossibile non sit, ut alio modo se habeant.
pass_a_gloss: But if anyone compare this moral certainty with those prior species of certainty, it must be confessed that it is of an inferior grade, and not in its own kind so great as is the certainty of science or of intelligence. For the intellect is more strongly and powerfully convinced of the truth of those things which it itself clearly and distinctly perceives, and whose contrary it sees to be plainly impossible, than of those which it judges and gathers so to stand from men’s constant fame and testimony, or from various signs and indications, although it is not absolutely impossible that they stand another way.
pass_b_english: Moral certainty < scientia / intelligentia in grade.
Clear distinct perception + plain impossibility of contrary convicts more strongly.
